tone_statements.citation: Zogbo, Lynell Marchese. 2019. Central vowels in the Kru language family: Innovation and areal spreading. In Emily Clem, Peter Jenks & Hannah Sande (eds.), Theory and description in African Linguistics: Selected papers from the 47th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 725-750. Berlin: Language Science Press.
tone_statements.quote: A typical system is seen in Kouya where vowels occur in two sets (Table 1, adapted from Saunders 2009: 50). [fn. 2:] As is traditional in Kru literature, in the examples to follow and throughout this paper, tones are marked by raised superscripts. Most Kru languages show four level tones: high (1), mid-high (2), mid (3), and low (4). Exceptionally Godié has only three level tones (high, mid, low), with only remnants of a fourth tone (Gratrix 1975). [Table 2: Kouya ±ATR sets] ɓʊ1lɛ2 'buffalo', tɪɓɛ33 'snake', mɪɔ13 'tear' (n.), mʊ3mɔɛ44 'smile' (v.), ɓʊɪ4 'flower'; di2de2 'father', ɓu2ɓui1 'smoke, vapor', ɓeli23 'brother', petu41 'grass', liɓo33 'work' (n.)

sources.note: Kouya appears in StressTyp2 only in the ISO language-name table (no stress record); not in WALS stress chapters (frame flags 0); PHOIBLE has no kouy1238 inventory.

sources.citation: Sande, Hannah. 2024. Insertion or deletion? CVCV/CCV alternations in Kru languages. In Ji Yea Kim et al. (eds.), Epenthesis and beyond, ch. 2. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Nothing on Kouya. Cites Saunders (2009) among data sources for the pan-Kru CVCV~CCV table (Table 11) but Kouya is not a row in the table and appears only on the map (Fig. 1). The word 'stress' occurs only for non-Kru comparison languages (Winnebago, SE Tepehuan, Tohono O'odham).

sources.citation: Sande, Hannah. 2018. Classification of Guebie within Kru. ACAL 47 proceedings chapter (Language Science Press); Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.1251712.
sources.note: Nothing on Kouya; Kouya appears only as a node under Eastern Bete in the family trees (Figs. 1-2). Phonology section (4.1 Tone) concerns Guebie (four tone heights) and Bete, not Kouya.

sources.citation: Gibbon, Dafydd. 2016. Legacy language atlas data mining: mapping Kru languages. Proceedings of LREC 2016 (paper 72).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Read only to check coverage of Marchese's Atlas linguistique kru (1984): the 19 atlas varieties listed (Aizi, Bassa, Bete, Cedepo, Dewoin, Dida de Lozoua, Dida F, Godie, Grebo, Guere, Klao, Koyo, Krahn, Kuwaa, Neyo, Niaboua, Seme, Tepo, Wobe) do not include Kouya, so the Atlas is not a Kouya source.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for kouy1238 (12 refs, downloaded via langdoc?languoids=kouy1238&cq=1): Saunders 2009; Saunders & Arthur 1996 Lexique (x2 records); Frick & Bolli 1971 Inventaire preliminaire; Arthur 1994, 1996, 1997 (ethnographic); Lowe, Arthur & Saunders 2003 (x2 records); three Kouya literacy primers 1995-1999 (SIL).
sources.note: Establishes that no phonology article, sketch, or SIL phonology statement for Kouya is registered in Glottolog/SIL bibliography (sil16 provider) other than the Saunders thesis.

sources.citation: kouya.net (Eddie Arthur's site 'Kouyanet'), Publications page and site searches for phonology / tone / grammar / Saunders.
sources.note: No linguistic papers on Kouya are hosted; the publications list contains Arthur 1993 (language learning, Notes on Linguistics) and Arthur 1996 (funerals, Notes on Anthropology) but no phonology.

It transcribes Kouya lexical items (from Saunders 2009: 50) with the Kru four-level numeral convention it defines (1 high, 2 mid-high, 3 mid, 4 low), and the Kouya forms use all four levels plus two-numeral sequences on one syllable (e.g. buu1le2 'buffalo', di2de2 'father', tIbE 33 'snake', bUI 4 'flower', mIO 13 'tear', beli 23 'brother', petu 41 'grass', kUa 11 'bone', kwlaa12 'tortoise') -- i.e. second-hand evidence that Saunders 2009 records Kouya as a four-height lexical tone language with contour sequences; the primary statement is in Saunders 2009 ch. o…
